subject: forensic-medicine
title: Entry and Exit Wounds, Kennedy Phenomenon and Ricochet

steps.title: The entry versus exit table
steps.tx: Examiners separate the two holes with the classic **entrance and exit wound differences**. Entry is smaller than the bullet, inverted, collared, less bloody, and may show burning, blackening or tattooing with cherry red tissues. Exit is bigger than the bullet, everted, puckered or torn, bloodier, with fat often protruding and no discharge marks at all. With high velocity bullets the two wounds may end up the same size, so no single trait decides alone.
steps.say: Small, inverted and collared means entry; large, everted and fatty means exit, judged as a pattern, not one trait.

steps.tx: Side by side, the two holes disagree on several points. **Entrance and exit wound differences** cover size, edge direction, bleeding and residue. Entry stays smaller than the bullet, with inverted margins, an abrasion collar, less blood, and sometimes burning, blackening or tattooing with cherry red tissue. Exit exceeds bullet diameter, looks everted, puckered or torn, bleeds more and may push fat outward, yet never carries powder marks. High velocity rounds can equalise the sizes, so one trait never decides direction alone.

steps.title: Why exits are larger and messier
steps.tx: By the time a bullet leaves, it may tumble, deform, fragment or carry bone chips ahead of it, producing the **large irregular exit wound**. Unsupported skin tears and breaks into pieces as the missile pushes out. Exit shapes vary through round, stellate, cruciate, elliptical and crescent forms, and head exits are usually star shaped like contact entries. A tumbling bullet exiting sideways can leave an elongated slit resembling a stab or incised wound.
steps.say: Tumbling, fragments and bone chips blast a wide torn exit, which on the head can star like a contact entry.

steps.title: When entry is larger than exit
steps.tx: The size rule reverses in defined situations collected as **large entry wound causes**: inrushing gases tear soft tissue at contact, a yawing or tumbling bullet strikes sideways, the bullet breaks with only part exiting, tangential entry avulses tissue, or the bullet enters through folded skin. Finding entry bigger than exit therefore does not overturn the diagnosis if inverted collared margins, discharge marks and an inward track all agree on the entry side.
steps.say: Gas tearing, yaw and skin folds can enlarge an entry beyond its exit, so margins and track outrank size alone.

steps.title: Single entry with multiple exits
steps.tx: One hole in and several out occurs when the **bullet fragments inside the body** into three or four pieces, each exiting separately. Bone struck on the way can shatter into secondary missiles that make their own exits. A jacket may separate from its core on a button, coin or bone, and each part cuts a separate track; with semi jacketed bullets the lead core usually exits while the jacket stays behind inside the body.
steps.say: Fragmenting bullets and bone chips multiply the exits from one entry, and a shed jacket often remains inside.

steps.title: Re entry wounds and missing bullets
steps.tx: A bullet crossing an arm and then the chest makes four wounds, and irregular surfaces such as breast or buttock can produce several exits and re entries in **multiple wound track puzzles**. The opposite puzzle also occurs: an entry with no bullet inside, because a bullet entering the stomach may be vomited, one in the windpipe coughed up, one in the mouth spat out, and one in the gut passed in faeces, or it may exit through its own entry hole.
steps.say: Count tracks, not holes, because limbs add re entries and swallowed or coughed bullets can vanish from the body.

nodes.label: X ray the whole body anyway

steps.title: Kennedy phenomenon, surgery erases the answer
steps.tx: Surgical alteration or suturing of gunshot wounds creates the **Kennedy phenomenon**: after emergency care, evaluation of whether a defect was entrance or exit becomes difficult or impossible. Wound excision, drain placement and stitching destroy collars, margins and discharge marks. The lesson for practice is to photograph and describe every wound before theatre whenever the patient's condition allows, and to record exactly what surgery changed.
steps.say: Once surgeons excise and stitch a gunshot wound its entry or exit nature may be lost, so document before theatre.

steps.title: Ricochet bullets arrive deformed
steps.tx: A **ricochet bullet** strikes an intervening hard surface first, rebounds at an angle smaller than its impact angle, and then hits the body. The critical angle for ricochet on hard surfaces is ten to thirty degrees. The bullet arrives deformed and flattened, gyroscopic spin lost, and makes a large irregular oval, triangular or cruciate entry with abraded margins, no abrasion collar and no burn marks. Soil, paint or fibres from the surface may cling to it.
steps.say: A bullet bounced at ten to thirty degrees arrives flattened and spinless, leaving a ragged collarless entry that mimics long range.

steps.tx: Beside an intact round sits a flattened, deformed projectile that hit something hard before the body. A **ricochet bullet** glances off at a rebound angle smaller than the angle of impact. On hard surfaces that critical angle lies between ten and thirty degrees. Gyroscopic spin is lost, so the wound is a large irregular oval, triangle or cross, with abraded edges, no abrasion collar and no burning. Soil, paint or fibres from the struck surface can stick on the metal.

steps.title: Internal ricochet inside the skull
steps.tx: A spent bullet that cannot pierce the far skull table can rebound off the inner table like a billiard ball in **internal ricochet**, cutting a second track through the brain, and occasionally a third. Entering at an acute angle, it may instead run along the dura, tearing leptomeninges and vessels in a shallow surface track. X ray and careful track dissection reveal these paths and fix the direction of fire inside the head.
steps.say: Bullets bounce off the inner skull table into second tracks, so an odd extra track does not mean a second shot.

nodes.label: Energy too low to exit skull

steps.title: Gutter wounds and grazes on the skull
steps.tx: A bullet striking the skull tangentially may carve entry and exit holes in the scalp two to three centimetres apart with an oval gutter in the bone between them, the **gutter or keyhole wound**. It may also deviate and run under the skin following the skull curvature for a considerable distance without penetrating. A still shallower strike makes a graze or slap: a reddish brown elliptical furrow with ecchymosed neighbouring skin and no perforation at all.
steps.say: Tangential bullets gutter the outer skull or merely slap a bruised furrow into scalp without entering the head.
